newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - Unfazed VA Tech says only way is up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Unfazed VA Tech says only way is up.

text.p: Austrian engineering group VA Tech AG, unfazed by higher taxes beleaguering the industry, on Wednesday said it should continue on its current roll, with higher growth expected in 1996 than 1995 due to record orders.
"We are counting on a very, very strong turnover boost for 1996 and 1997 which will also affect the results," chief financial officer Helmut Hamminger told a news conference.

Pre-tax profit in the first six months surged 50 percent to 484 million schillings ($45.49 million), while sales jumped 32 percent to 12.2 billion -- both figures far exceeding analysts' expectations.
Net profit rose to 378 million from 294 million in the year-ago period in spite of the fact the company is now paying around 20 percent in tax on profits, compared with 10 percent a year ago.
The company attributed the strong earnings to a surge in orders, with the order intake jumping 20 percent to 20.3 billion schillings from 17 billion in the same period last year.
VA Tech said it expected to post double-digit growth in all key earnings apart from net profit, which would come under pressure from higher taxes for 1996 and 1997.

"There is a good chance we will have higher growth in 1996 than we had from 1994 to 1995," said chief executive Othmar Puehringer. In 1995, pre-tax profit jumped 12.8 percent to 1.27 billion schillings.
But chief financial officer Hamminger cautioned growth would be more moderate than that in the first half of the year.
The Austrian government earlier this year announced it was scrapping tax credits on losses carried forward in 1996 and 1997 which has hit net profits across the industry.
Puehringer said the company would continue its shareholder-friendly dividend policy. "There will be no reduction in dividend plus bonus," he said. The dividend currently stands at 28 schillings.
He said the company's strategic focus on three key areas -- metallurgical engineering, energy and environmental engineering and plant engineering -- had been effective.
Plant engineering and services, reported a whopping 48 percent growth in new orders, accounted for just under half of the order intake.

This was in part due to the acquisition of Lentjes Anlagen und Rohrleitungsbau GmbH in Germany last year, the company said. The acquisition helped boost the order intake in Western Europe to 41 percent from 21 percent, it noted.
Orders in metallurgical engineering and energy and environmental engineering grew by six and three percent respectively.
Orders on hand also achieved record levels, reaching 76 billion schillings against 64 billion in the first half of 1995, the company said.
VA Tech shares gained 9.5 schillings to 1,340 in an overall limp Vienna market. ($1=10.64 Schilling)
